master.title: News reports in Russia: Units of Russian Western, Southern Military Districts heading back to base after exercise
master.content:
Units of Russian Western, Southern Military Districts heading back to base after exercise

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - Units of Russia's Western and Southern Military Districts are heading back to base by rail and by truck at the conclusion of their training, the Russian Defense Ministry said on Tuesday.

"Units of the Southern and Western Military Districts, which have accomplished their missions, are boarding trains and trucks and will head for their garrisons later today. Some units will join military convoys and will perform self-propelled marches," Russian Defense Ministry spokesman Igor Konashenkov said.

Russian Defense Ministry releases video of armored vehicles returning to base from exercises

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - Russian armored vehicles are returning to base from exercises, the Russian Defense Ministry said in a video released on Tuesday.

The video features an off-road march of tanks, as well as tanks, infantry combat vehicles and self-propelled artillery systems being loaded onto a train.

Russia continuing military exercises involving practically all districts, fleets - Defense Ministry

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - Russian troops are continuing exercises in a number of operative sectors, Russian Defense Ministry spokesman Igor Konashenkov said.

"The Russian Armed Forces are continuing a number of large-scale exercises that involve practically all military districts, fleets and the Airborne Forces," Konashenkov told reporters on Tuesday.

Forces from the Eastern Military District and the Airborne Forces, which are taking part in the Union Resolve exercise, are training for a defensive operation aimed to deter an aggression against the Union State together with the Belarusian Armed Forces, he said.

"Meanwhile, a series of naval drills involving surface ships, submarines and marine aviation are taking place in operative sectors of the world's oceans, and the seas adjoining Russian territory," Konashenkov said.

Military attaches accredited in Minsk invited to Russia-Belarus live-fire exercise as observers - Russian Defense Ministry

MOSCOW. Feb 15 (Interfax) - Foreign observers have been invited to maneuvers as part of the ongoing Russian-Belarusian military exercise, Russian Defense Ministry spokesman Igor Konashenkov said.

"Military attaches in charge of defense issues representing foreign states' embassies in the Republic of Belarus and the media have been invited to practical maneuvers as observers," Konashenkov said.

The aforementioned live-fire exercise will be conducted at the Obuz-Lesnovsky range on February 16, he said.

"A marine brigade acting together with military units of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Belarus and backed by tactical and army air force planes will simulate a defensive battle and will conduct maneuvers in other sectors during the exercise," Konashenkov said.
